name: Abraham
who: herdsman of Ur and Haran, called out to Canaan

pace.did: He left Haran with his household when he was told to go.
He rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey and set out for the place he had been told of.
pace.quote: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey

voice.did: He came near and put his objection about Sodom to God out loud.
He kept pressing the same question down from fifty to ten.

lead.did: He led out three hundred and eighteen of his own men, pursued as far as Dan and brought back Lot and the goods.
He let Lot pick his half of the land first and took whatever was left.

conflict.did: He proposed a separation to Lot to end the quarrel between their herdsmen.
conflict.quote: Please, let there be no strife between you and me

conflict.did: He stood between Sodom and its judgement and argued for the city.

doubt.did: He asked for something to go on before accepting the promise of the land.
doubt.quote: Lord GOD, how will I know that I will inherit it?

doubt.did: He fell on his face and laughed, asking whether a hundred-year-old man would have a child.
He took the word about his offspring as it stood.

plan.did: He split the wood for the offering and saddled the donkey before leaving.
He went up the mountain carrying fire and wood and no animal, telling Isaac one would be provided.

name: Moses
who: raised in Pharaoh's house, shepherd in Midian, leader of Israel out of Egypt

pace.did: He looked both ways, killed the Egyptian he had seen striking a Hebrew and hid the body in the sand.
He raised objection after objection at the bush before going, and asked for someone else to be sent.
pace.quote: Oh, Lord, please send someone else.

voice.did: He put his objection to God out loud as soon as he was sent.
voice.quote: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh

voice.did: He argued out loud with God for the people after the calf.

lead.did: He went in to Pharaoh himself and delivered the demand to let the people go.
He chose able men, made them rulers over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and let them judge the small cases.

conflict.did: He went to Pharaoh with the demand and kept coming back with it.
He threw down the tablets, burnt the calf, ground it to powder and made the people drink it.
He went between God and the people and asked for the people to be spared.

doubt.did: He said the people would not believe him and would say the LORD had not appeared to him.
He asked how flocks and herds or all the fish of the sea could feed six hundred thousand men for a month.

plan.did: He set up a standing order of rulers so that cases were judged at all times and only hard ones came to him.
With no water for the people he took the elders and the rod and struck the rock he was shown.

name: Joseph
who: eleventh son of Jacob, sold into Egypt, then set over its grain

pace.did: He set out a fourteen-year scheme of storage and appointment before anything was done.
He recognised his brothers and dealt with them as a stranger instead of saying who he was.
pace.quote: acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them

voice.did: He kept his identity from his brothers through several meetings.
He turned away from them to weep, then came back, spoke to them and bound Simeon in front of them.
He told his brothers the dream about their sheaves bowing to his.

lead.did: The keeper of the prison put every prisoner and everything done there into his hand.
He gathered the food of seven years and stored it city by city until he stopped counting.

conflict.did: He told the brothers who had sold him not to be grieved or angry with themselves.
He promised to provide for them and their little ones, and spoke kindly to them.
He took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: He proposed taking a fifth of the produce through seven plenteous years against seven years of famine.
He carried the storage out himself, laying up grain in each city from the fields around it.

name: David
who: shepherd of Bethlehem, harpist, outlaw captain, king of Israel

pace.did: He ran towards the Philistine line to meet Goliath.
pace.quote: David hurried and ran towards the army to meet the Philistine

pace.did: He called for the ephod and asked whether to pursue before he went after the raiders.

voice.did: He told Saul in front of the camp that he would go and fight the Philistine.
He made a lament over Saul and Jonathan and had it taught to Judah.
He danced before the ark in the sight of the whole procession.

lead.did: Four hundred men in distress, in debt and discontented gathered to him at the cave and he became their captain.
He put himself forward as the one who would fight when no one else would.

conflict.did: He went out to meet the Philistine in single combat and struck him with a stone.
He came out of the cave, called after Saul and showed him the cut skirt instead of the body.
He stopped Abishai from striking the sleeping Saul.

doubt.did: He asked whether he would overtake the raiders before setting out after them.
When the child died he got up, washed, worshipped and ate, and said he could not bring him back.

plan.did: He gathered materials for the house to be built after him.
plan.quote: So David prepared abundantly before his death.

plan.did: He arrived at Nob with nothing and asked for five loaves or whatever was available.
He had come away without his sword or weapons and had to ask what was there.
plan.quote: I haven’t brought my sword or my weapons with me

name: Jonathan
who: eldest son of Saul, soldier, David's covenant friend

pace.did: He crossed over to the Philistine garrison with his armour bearer and told no one, including his father.
He proposed the crossing on the spot and went.

voice.did: He went over to the garrison without telling his father.
He passed the warning to David through arrows so that even the boy with him knew nothing.
voice.quote: Only Jonathan and David knew the matter.

voice.did: He spoke to Saul directly on David's behalf.

lead.did: He took off his own robe, clothing, sword, bow and sash and gave them to David.
He went out to David in the woods and told him he would be king and that he himself would be next to him.

conflict.did: He put David's case to Saul until Saul swore David would not be put to death.
He offered to do whatever David asked while David was hunted by his father.

doubt.did: He crossed to the garrison saying only that it might be that the LORD would work for them.
doubt.quote: It may be that the LORD will work for us

plan.did: He kept an appointed time in the field and used an arrow signal agreed in advance.
He went over to the garrison with one man and no arrangement of any kind.

name: Elijah
who: prophet of Gilead in the days of Ahab

pace.did: He walked in on Ahab and announced that there would be no dew or rain.
When he heard Jezebel's threat he got up and ran for his life to Beersheba.

voice.did: He put the choice to the assembled people out loud.
voice.quote: How long will you waver between the two sides?

voice.did: At noon he mocked the prophets of Baal in front of the crowd.

lead.did: He called all the people over to him and repaired the altar in front of them.
He went over to Elisha at the plough and put his own mantle on him.

conflict.did: He called the people and the prophets of Baal together to settle the question in public.
He met Ahab after Naboth's death and told him to his face what he had done.

doubt.did: He asked God why evil had come on the widow he was staying with.
He went to the brook Cherith and lived there as he had been told.

plan.did: He lived at the brook on bread and meat brought to him morning and evening.
plan.quote: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening

plan.did: He arrived at Zarephath with nothing and asked a widow gathering sticks for water and a morsel of bread.
He went a day's journey into the wilderness with no provision, lay down under a tree and was woken to eat.

name: Nehemiah
who: cupbearer to Artaxerxes, then governor over the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall

pace.did: On hearing about the wall he sat down, wept and mourned for several days before doing anything.
He was in Jerusalem three days, then rode out at night to inspect the broken walls before saying a word about his plan.

voice.did: He kept his intention for Jerusalem to himself while he surveyed the ground.
voice.quote: I didn’t tell anyone what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem

voice.did: The rulers, priests, nobles and workers were still not told where he had been or what he had done.
He called a great assembly and charged the nobles and rulers with usury in front of it.

lead.did: He stationed the people by family with swords, spears and bows and addressed the nobles, rulers and the rest himself.
He split his servants between the work and the weapons and kept the trumpeter beside him.

conflict.did: He contended with the nobles and rulers over what they were charging their brothers.
He contended with the men who had married foreign wives and struck some of them.
conflict.quote: I contended with them, cursed them, struck certain of them, plucked off their hair

conflict.did: He refused four invitations to meet Sanballat and Geshem in the plain of Ono.

doubt.did: He questioned the men who came from Judah about the survivors and about Jerusalem before acting.
He answered the opposition by starting to build.

plan.did: He set the king a return date and asked in advance for letters to the governors and timber from the king's forest.
He arranged the work so half the men built while half stood armed.

name: Daniel
who: exile of Judah, trained for the Babylonian court, reader of the king's dreams

pace.did: He went in and asked the king to appoint him a time before he would give the interpretation.
He proposed a ten-day trial of vegetables and water to the steward rather than refusing the food outright.

voice.did: He was troubled by the vision and said nothing of it to anyone.
voice.quote: I kept the matter in my heart

voice.did: He told Nebuchadnezzar to his face to break off his sins.
He refused Belshazzar's gifts and read the writing anyway.

lead.did: He went home and told Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah so they would ask for mercy along with him.
He asked the king to put Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego over the affairs of the province.

conflict.did: He found the steward a way to test the diet without either of them being endangered.
He gave the king counsel the king had not asked for.

doubt.did: He went up to one of those standing by and asked what the vision meant.
When the decree was signed he went home and prayed at his open windows three times a day as he had before.

plan.did: He settled beforehand what he would not eat and then made his request.
He kept a fixed practice of three set times a day, windows open towards Jerusalem.

name: John the Baptist
who: preacher in the wilderness of Judea who baptised in the Jordan

pace.did: The text does not show this.

voice.did: He said what he thought of the Pharisees and Sadducees to their faces as they came.
He told Herod that his marriage to Herodias was not lawful.
voice.quote: It is not lawful for you to have her.

lead.did: He pointed two of his own disciples at Jesus and they left him and followed Jesus.
He said his own part was to become less as the other became greater.
lead.quote: He must increase, but I must decrease.

conflict.did: He challenged the Pharisees and Sadducees who had come out to him.
He told the king to his face that he was in the wrong, and was arrested for it.

doubt.did: From prison he sent two disciples to ask Jesus directly whether he was the one to come.
doubt.quote: Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?

plan.did: He lived in the wilderness on what it gave him.
plan.quote: His food was locusts and wild honey.

plan.did: He wore camel's hair and a leather belt and ate locusts and wild honey.

name: Peter
who: fisherman of Galilee, one of the Twelve

pace.did: He asked to be called out onto the water, and on the one word stepped down from the boat.
Told it was the Lord on the shore, he pulled his coat on and threw himself into the sea.
He drew a sword in the garden and struck the high priest's servant.

voice.did: He took Jesus aside and began to rebuke him for what he had just said.
On the mountain he proposed building three tents.
He stood up with the eleven and addressed the crowd at Jerusalem.

lead.did: He stood up in the middle of about a hundred and twenty disciples and spoke.
He said he was going fishing and the others went with him.

conflict.did: He charged Ananias with the lie in front of the assembly.
He rebuked Jesus over what he had said about Jerusalem.
When those of the circumcision contended with him he explained what had happened in order.

doubt.did: He refused the vision's instruction, saying he had never eaten anything common or unclean.
He asked how many times he had to forgive and proposed a number.
He left the boat on a single word.

plan.did: He answered the tax collectors yes with nothing in hand and was sent to find the coin in a fish's mouth.
He announced he was going fishing that night with nothing arranged.
He told the man at the gate he had no silver or gold.

name: Paul
who: Pharisee of Tarsus, tentmaker, apostle to the nations

pace.did: After the night vision the party immediately looked for a way over to Macedonia.
He went into Arabia and back to Damascus and let three years pass before going up to Jerusalem.

voice.did: He argued in the synagogue and in the Athens marketplace with whoever was there, every day.
He opposed Peter in public at Antioch.
voice.quote: I resisted him to his face

lead.did: He picked Silas and set out on his own circuit.
He fixed the party's route past Ephesus to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost.

conflict.did: He held his position about Mark until he and Barnabas separated.
conflict.quote: the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other

conflict.did: He confronted Peter rather than raising it privately.

doubt.did: He was told to get up and go into the city and be told there what to do, and he went.
He went up to Jerusalem after everyone present had begged him not to.
He asked three times for the thing to be taken away before he stopped asking.

plan.did: He had settled the sailing route in advance so as not to spend time in Asia.
He wrote ahead about a journey to Spain and about being helped on his way by the Romans.

name: Thomas
who: one of the Twelve, also called Didymus

pace.did: When Jesus turned back towards Judea he said at once that they should go too.
pace.quote: Let’s also go, that we may die with him.

pace.did: He would not act on the other disciples' report until he had seen and touched for himself.

voice.did: He said out loud that they did not know where Jesus was going or how they could know the way.
He said to the other disciples what he thought the journey to Judea would cost.

lead.did: He addressed his fellow disciples and told them what they should do.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: He named the evidence he required before he would believe the report.
doubt.quote: Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.

doubt.did: He said he did not know the way and asked how he could.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

name: Deborah
who: prophetess who judged Israel and summoned Barak against Sisera

pace.did: She sat under the palm between Ramah and Bethel and Israel came up to her for judgement.
She sent for Barak and gave him his orders.

voice.did: She told Barak the mountain, the tribes, the number of men and where Sisera would be drawn.
She sang the account of the battle publicly that same day with Barak.

lead.did: She told Barak to go down, and ten thousand men went after him.
lead.quote: Go; for this is the day

lead.did: She agreed to go with Barak and told him plainly the honour would not be his.

conflict.did: She directed a muster against Sisera and his chariots.
She sent the army down the mountain to engage.

doubt.did: She passed on the command without asking for anything further to go on.
doubt.quote: Hasn’t the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded

doubt.did: She named the day as the day of victory before the battle was fought.

plan.did: She set the ground, the river, the two tribes and the number of men before the muster began.

name: Esther
who: Jewish orphan raised by Mordecai, made queen of Persia

pace.did: She called a three-day fast before going in to the king.
Asked at the first banquet what she wanted, she asked only for a second banquet the next day.

voice.did: She did not tell anyone in the palace who her people were.
voice.quote: Esther had not made known her people nor her relatives

voice.did: She still had not made it known after she was made queen.

lead.did: She ordered the fast in Susa and Mordecai did everything she had commanded him.
She asked the king to have letters written reversing Haman's.

conflict.did: She named Haman as the enemy while he was sitting at the table.
conflict.quote: An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!

conflict.did: She asked for the decree in Susa to run a further day.

doubt.did: She set out the law about the inner court and the thirty days before she would agree to go.

plan.did: She prepared one banquet, then a second, and made her request only at the second.
She fixed the three days of fasting for herself, her maidens and the Jews of Susa first.

name: Ruth
who: Moabite widow who went with Naomi to Bethlehem

pace.did: She proposed going out to glean and went that day.
She went down to the threshing floor and did everything she had been told.

voice.did: She said out loud, to Naomi's face, that she would not turn back.

lead.did: She carried the barley into the city and gave Naomi what she had left over from her own meal.
She left her own country and people to stay with her mother-in-law.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: She agreed to the threshing-floor plan without asking anything about it.
doubt.quote: All that you say, I will do.

plan.did: She went out to glean behind whoever would let her and came to the part of the field that belonged to Boaz.
She gleaned from the morning until the evening and took home what that day gave.

name: Hannah
who: wife of Elkanah of Ramathaim, mother of Samuel

pace.did: She stayed behind from the yearly journey and waited until the child was weaned before bringing him.

voice.did: She prayed at the doorpost without making a sound.
voice.quote: Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard.

voice.did: When she brought Samuel up she prayed out loud in the house.

lead.did: The text does not show this.

conflict.did: Accused by Eli of being drunk, she answered him about herself and made no charge back.

doubt.did: After Eli's word she went away, ate, and was no longer sad, with nothing yet changed.

plan.did: She brought three bulls, an ephah of meal and a container of wine with the child.
She made him a little robe and brought it up to him year after year.

name: Abigail
who: wife of Nabal of Carmel, later wife of David

pace.did: Told what her husband had done, she loaded bread, wine, sheep, grain, raisins and figs onto donkeys straight away.
pace.quote: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread

pace.did: She got down off the donkey as soon as she saw David and went to the ground in front of him.

voice.did: She asked David to hear her and then made her whole case to him.
She told Nabal nothing about it until the next morning.

lead.did: She sent her young men on ahead with the loaded donkeys and followed after them.
lead.quote: But she didn’t tell her husband, Nabal.

conflict.did: She put herself between David's four hundred men and her husband's household and took the blame on herself.
David said she had kept him that day from blood guiltiness and from avenging himself.

doubt.did: When David's servants came for her she got up and rode away with them the same hour.

plan.did: She gathered and loaded a full train of provisions before setting out to meet David.

name: Rahab
who: of Jericho, a prostitute whose house stood on the city wall, who hid Joshua's two spies

pace.did: When the king's men came to the door she had already taken the two men and hidden them.
She let them down by a cord through the window that night.

voice.did: She told the king's messengers the men had left at dark while they were on her roof.
She told the two spies what the city had heard about the Red Sea and about Sihon and Og.

lead.did: She told the spies where to go and how many days to stay hidden.
She required an oath from them for her father, mother, brothers and sisters before they left.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: She acted on a report of the Red Sea and the two kings that she had only heard.

plan.did: Two strangers came to her house that evening and she hid them under flax on the roof when the search arrived.
The scarlet line in the window was the spies' condition, given to her as they left.

name: Mary of Nazareth
who: mother of Jesus

pace.did: At the greeting she turned it over and worked out what kind of greeting it was before answering.
She got up in those days and went into the hill country in haste.

voice.did: After the shepherds came she kept what was said to herself and turned it over.
voice.quote: Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.

voice.did: After Jerusalem she again kept what had been said in her heart.

lead.did: At the wedding she pointed the servants at her son rather than directing them herself.
lead.quote: Whatever he says to you, do it.

lead.did: She was the one who raised the shortage of wine.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: She asked how what she had been told could happen.
doubt.quote: How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?

doubt.did: She accepted it after the one answer and the angel left.
doubt.quote: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

name: Martha
who: of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, who received Jesus into her house

pace.did: With Jesus in the house she was straight into the serving.
pace.quote: Martha was distracted with much serving

pace.did: Hearing Jesus was coming she went out and met him while her sister stayed in the house.

voice.did: She took her complaint about her sister straight to Jesus in the room.
At the tomb she said out loud what four days would have done to the body.
voice.quote: Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.

lead.did: She was the one who received him into the house.
She asked Jesus to tell her sister to come and help.

conflict.did: She raised the division of the work in front of everyone rather than with her sister alone.

doubt.did: Asked directly whether she believed, she said she did, with her brother still in the tomb.
When the stone was to be moved she objected on the facts of the fourth day.

plan.did: She laid on a full meal for the visitors.
At the supper made for him in Bethany she served.

name: Mary Magdalene
who: of Magdala, out of whom seven demons had gone, first at the empty tomb

pace.did: She went to the tomb early, while it was still dark.
Seeing the stone moved she ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple.
pace.quote: she ran and came to Simon Peter

voice.did: She went to the disciples and told them what she had seen and what had been said to her.
Asked why she was weeping, she said plainly that the body had been taken and she did not know where.

lead.did: The text does not show this.

conflict.did: The text does not show this.

doubt.did: Taking the man for the gardener, she asked where the body had been put so she could take it away.
When he said her name she turned and answered him at once.

plan.did: When the Sabbath was past she bought spices with the other women to go and anoint him.
plan.quote: bought spices, that they might come and anoint him

plan.did: The women who had come from Galilee marked where the body was laid, then went and prepared spices and ointments.

name: Priscilla
who: tentmaker of Rome and Corinth, who worked and taught with her husband Aquila

pace.did: The text does not show this.

voice.did: Hearing Apollos, she and Aquila set out to him what he had left out rather than letting it stand.

lead.did: She and Aquila took Apollos aside and set out the way of God to him more accurately.
lead.quote: they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately

lead.did: Paul greets her and Aquila as fellow workers who risked their own necks for his life.

conflict.did: She took Apollos aside instead of correcting him in the synagogue where he was speaking.

doubt.did: The text does not show this.

plan.did: The text does not show this.

name: Jesus
who: of Nazareth, whose acts here are taken only from the four Gospels

pace.did: Asked by the leper, he stretched out his hand and touched him there and then.
He was on the mountain all night before he called his disciples at daybreak and chose twelve of them.
Hearing that Lazarus was ill he stayed two days where he was before going.
pace.quote: he stayed two days in the place where he was

voice.did: Questioned by the high priest he said his teaching had all been done in public.
voice.quote: I spoke openly to the world.

voice.did: He told the disciples what was coming in Jerusalem without softening it.
Before Pilate, with the charges being read, he gave no further answer.
voice.quote: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marvelled.

lead.did: On the road up to Jerusalem he walked ahead of the Twelve and they followed.
lead.quote: Jesus was going in front of them

lead.did: At supper he took a towel and a basin and washed the disciples' feet.
He sent the Twelve out in pairs without him and gave them his own authority.

conflict.did: He made a whip of cords, drove the traders and animals out of the temple and overturned the money changers' tables.
From the cross he asked that the men carrying out the execution be forgiven.
After Peter had denied him he asked him three times and gave him the flock to feed.

doubt.did: As a boy he sat among the teachers in the temple, listening to them and putting questions to them.
In the garden he prayed a second time and went on without the answer he had asked for.
He told Peter to put up the sword and took what was coming.

plan.did: He sent two disciples with instructions about a man with a pitcher and an upper room, and they found it as he had said.
He sent Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal.
With a crowd, no food and the day gone, he asked how many loaves there were and used the five and the two fish.
